statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-5773: libcurl can reuse an SMB connection for a transfer that should use a different share on the same server, so a file can be downloaded from or uploaded to the wrong place (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-5773.html). It affects curl 7.40.0 to 8.19.0 and was fixed in curl 8.20.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/74a169575d6412dc0ff532acdf94de35a6c2a571, which disables connection reuse for SMB and SMBS; curl 8.20.0 also made SMB support opt-in, and curl 8.23.0 dropped it. As of 2026-11-27 the DHI Alpine 3.23 main repository publishes curl builds 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0, 8.19.0-r0, 8.20.0-r0, 8.20.0-r1, 8.21.0-r0, 8.22.0-r0, 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1, and the version string in each build's libcurl matches its package version. In the static libcurl.a shipped in curl-static, on x86_64 and aarch64, 8.17.0-r1, 8.18.0-r0 and 8.19.0-r0 build the SMB protocol (the object built from smb.c defines 14 functions), and in 8.18.0-r0 and 8.19.0-r0 the SMB and SMBS protocol entries set the connection-reuse flag (8.17.0-r1 is curl 8.17.0, which has no such flag and which curl lists as affected). From 8.20.0-r0 to 8.22.0-r0 the object built from smb.c defines no functions and the SMB and SMBS entries no longer set the connection-reuse flag, and 8.23.0-r0 and 8.23.0-r1 have no SMB entries at all. So 8.20.0-r0, the first build of curl 8.20.0, is the first fixed build.

CVE-2026-5773: libcurl can reuse an SMB connection for a transfer that should use a different share on the same server, so a file can be downloaded from or uploaded to the wrong place (https://curl.se/docs/CVE-2026-5773.html). It affects curl 7.40.0 to 8.19.0 and was fixed in curl 8.20.0 by https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/74a169575d6412dc0ff532acdf94de35a6c2a571, which disables connection reuse for SMB and SMBS; curl 8.20.0 also made SMB support opt-in, and curl 8.23.0 dropped it. Debian backported the fix to trixie in 8.14.1-2+deb13u4 (https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-5773). The DHI curl packages for Debian 13 are rebuilds of Debian's trixie curl 8.14.1-2; as of 2026-11-27 the DHI Debian repository publishes three of them (the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5 and two rebuilds of 8.14.1-2+deb13u7) for amd64 and arm64, all later than 8.14.1-2+deb13u4, and each ships a Debian changelog that records the fix under 8.14.1-2+deb13u4. Debian builds SMB support. In libcurl4t64 and libcurl3t64-gnutls of all three builds, on amd64 and arm64, the SMB connect function marks every new SMB connection for closing (it calls Curl_conncontrol with CONNCTRL_CONNECTION), which is what the backported fix does instead of keeping the connection for reuse; in Debian's own unfixed 8.14.1-2+deb13u3 libcurl4t64 build (amd64) the same call keeps the connection (CONNCTRL_KEEP). Every published build carries the fix, so the fixed version is the lowest published one, the rebuild of 8.14.1-2+deb13u5.
